title: Integrality Gap of Sharp Variance Bounds for Multi-Arm Contrasts in Finite Populations
banked_reason: D0.5.G: delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field; the note proves the advertised sharp order, not the exact frontier, and two local panel findings remain unrepaired, so mathematical soundness is not established.
gap_reasons: The note proves the advertised sharp order, not the exact frontier: it establishes a same-class 1/N bracket, while the limit of N Delta_N and the extremal constant remain open.
The universal upper constant is extremely loose—402/N is weaker than the trivial bound until N=1609—and the resulting O(N^-2) variance correction is dominated by the proved sampling error.

The exact-rational polynomial-time claim is supported only by a compressed freezing/tree-matching specification and a high-level bit-growth argument, without executable pseudocode, implementation, or the cited rational verification checks needed for reproducibility.
HALTED AT TRIAGE: the math panel returned revise and its findings were never repaired, so this note is NOT established as mathematically sound.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a same-class Θ(1/N) realizability-gap bracket, strengthened the upper constant from 3456 to 402, and generalized the argument to an arbitrary-K scalar rank-one contrast support-size dichotomy with explicit padded lower witnesses. The field claim failed because the exact normalized frontier remains open, the finite-N certificate is loose and practically dominated by sampling error, and the implementation/comparator evidence stayed compressed. Triage also stopped before two local math-panel findings were repaired, so this bank entry records useful derivations but not an established sound theorem package.
tldr: For scalar rank-one squared-contrast transport with any fixed number \(K\) of empirical marginals and fixed coefficient vector \(\widetilde c\), the same-\(N\) realization loss has an exact support-size phase transition: it is zero when at most two coefficients are nonzero and is \(\Theta_{\widetilde c}(N^{-1})\) when at least three are nonzero.  Ordered dual-slope roots of lengths \(H_j=2\|\widetilde c\|_1-|\widetilde c_j|\), active-arm basic-table freezing, and hierarchical repair give the explicit upper constant \((16r^2/3)\sum_jH_j^2\), while affine placement of the padded four-row obstruction gives \(5\lambda_{\widetilde c}^2/N\) on every \(N\ge4\).  For the causal contrast \(c=(1/4,1/4,-1/2)\), the upper constant is exactly \(402\) and the transferred lower constant improves incidentally to \(5/215296\).  The complete-randomization application remains the original three-arm finite-population variance certificate, whose deterministic realization width is \(O(N^{-2})\); sampling-without-replacement uncertainty remains separate and larger.
gap: Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) formulate causal variance bounds over fractional multi-marginal couplings, whereas a finite population requires one common \(N\)-row schedule. Emami and Pass (2025) demonstrate discrete non-Monge optimality and request quantitative error bounds, but in a different quadratic orientation. Haus (2015) treats exact mixability and bottleneck approximation, and Brennan et al. (2025) rely on integer programming without an analytic realization width.
fill: The project derives an ordered dual-slope interval lemma, a multiscale exact-marginal repair algorithm, an all-\(N\) rational lower family, and design-based endpoint certificates with explicit sampling-without-replacement plug-in error.
